review.headline: A hidden Goose flipped every round, and nobody at the table noticed.
review.summary: In round 1, four honest Farm Geese suspected each other while two Cat Burglers kept quiet. The table eggsecuted Drew, whose net-zero report was true. Round 2 had no Meowfia at all. The table eggsecuted Blair for a Lyrebird story that was actually correct, and Ellis banked 21 points. In round 3, Alex openly claimed a cat role and nobody punished it. The table caught Drew, a real Meowfia, but the Goose was still in the pool and inverted scoring, so the four Meowfia won and the two Farm players who voted correctly lost. Ellis won 36 to 26 mostly through that one round 2 throw, without ever reasoning about the Goose.

rounds.recap: All four Farm players were Geese and all four claimed it truthfully, but the table assumed someone was lying. Drew took three Goose eggs and lost three to Casey's Cat Burgler steal, so his report honestly read 'no change' and looked like a lie. Drew was eggsecuted 9 votes to 2. He was Farm, but the Goose inverted scoring, so Farm won anyway.

No Meowfia this round. Angel's Trumpet turned visits into steals, and Casey's Brumby moved every animal one seat. Blair gained a capped +5 as Lyrebird, explained the cap correctly, and was eggsecuted 7 to 3 for a 'shifting story'. With the Goose inversion, everyone won and kept their thrown cards.

Four of six players were Meowfia. Drew and Ellis checked each other as House Cats, and Casey confirmed Alex as Cat Burgler. Drew's correct count was 'corrected' by Blair's misreading of the record, and Drew was eggsecuted 5 to 2. Farm caught a real Meowfia, but the Goose inversion handed the round to Meowfia. Under Corpse Flower, nobody at the table ever found out.

highlights.text: Four players claimed Goose and all four were telling the truth. The table eggsecuted the one whose report was most honest.
With no Meowfia in play, Ellis threw an 11 and a 10 at an innocent Blair and banked 21 points, which decided the game.
Drew and Ellis, both House Cats, visited each other. Each learned the other was a teammate, and Ellis spent the day steering votes toward Blair.
Alex opened with 'Alex here, Cat Burgler', which openly names a Meowfia role. Nobody voted for him.

confusions.what: Said a Goose visit can't give Ellis 3 eggs. Ellis was legitimately hit by three Goose visits.
Said Drew should be at 7. He ignored Drew's own Goose egg and any steals, and never considered a Cat Burgler.
Said Drew went from 6 to 5. Drew started at 5.
Said Drew's visit 'didn't land on me like I expected'. It did. Ellis misread his own +3.
Said Ellis's +3 from a visit on Drew was impossible. Three separate Goose visits explained it.
Nobody remembered that the Goose in the pool swaps winners and losers at scoring. It stayed in the pool all game and flipped every round.
Said Blair's Lyrebird gain should equal Casey's 9. He forgot the 5-egg nightly cap.
Said Ellis's Pigeon visit should lay an egg in Ellis's own nest. A Pigeon lays in the target's nest.
Put his -2 down to two Pigeon steals. It was three steals (including Alex's Goose) offset by his own steal from Blair.
Said Drew's nest also dropped. Drew's was unchanged.
Treated Drew's change from Pigeon to Brumby as a suspicious story change. It was a legitimate Brumby rotation.
Treated Ellis claiming Goose in round 1 and Pigeon in round 2 as a contradiction. Roles are re-dealt every round.
Said House Cat wasn't in play, so his Crane egg went to his own nest. Three House Cats were in play, and his visit stole from Drew.
Misstated the Crane rule, saying a named animal not in play shouldn't put an egg in the Crane's own nest.
Thought his Cat Burgler visit did nothing and said he 'chose to steal 0'. Under Angel's Trumpet his steal of 3 laid 3 eggs in Finley's nest.
Openly claimed Cat Burgler, which is a Meowfia role. Nobody at the table picked up on it.
Compared Drew's nest of 2 to the previous day's 5 and ignored the 2 cards he threw. Drew really lost only 1 overnight.
Misread the record and told Drew his 2 Wilds were thrown in round 1. Drew's first account was correct, and Blair pushed him into a needless correction.

design_notes: The Goose's scoring inversion is permanent once revealed, and it decided all three rounds while no player ever mentioned it. In round 3 the Farm players who found a real Meowfia lost. A rule this big needs a reminder from the Storyteller at every vote, or it should last only one round.

Dawn reports only give the net change. Drew's +3/-3 showed up as 'no change', which hid the Cat Burgler completely and got an honest player eggsecuted. Reporting eggs laid and eggs taken separately would make theft a clue instead of a perfect alibi.
The deck ran out by round 3 night. Lyrebird hit the +5 cap twice. Blair and Finley gained nothing in round 3. Shuffle discards back in, or reduce big self-laying effects like Lyrebird.

Round 2 had no Meowfia and no Cactus Flower, but the Goose inversion still made everyone a winner, and it produced the game's biggest score (Ellis 21). No-Meowfia rounds should not be the best rounds to throw high cards.

Twinflower, Angel's Trumpet, Brumby, then Angel's Trumpet again with Crane and Corpse Flower piled up modifiers until no claim could be checked. Players defaulted to 'whose story shifted' and voted out truth-tellers twice. Brumby's rotation was never discussed, and an open Cat Burgler claim went unnoticed. Mark cats clearly, and cap active modifiers per round.
